subject: [PATCH v1 2/3] mm: memcg: read root lruvec LRU stats from the node counters

reviews.author: Yosry Ahmed
reviews.summary: Reviewer Yosry Ahmed suggested that the patch could be simplified by directly using the node counters in lruvec_page_state() and lruvec_page_state_monotonic(), as these functions already fallback to node stats when memcg is disabled. They asked if there are cases where the node stats would not be suitable.
reviews.raw_body:
Why not do this directly in lruvec_page_state() and
lruvec_page_state_monotonic()? They already fallback to node stats if
memcg is disabled, why not do the same for the root? Are there cases
where the node stats are not the right thing to do?

reviews.author: Joanne Koong (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that there are cases where node counters and root memcg stats may not be equal, specifically citing slab's NR_SLAB_RECLAIMABLE_B and NR_SLAB_UNRECLAIMABLE_B statistics, and explained that this is due to the way slab pages are accounted for in the node counter but only updated in the memcg stats under certain conditions.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Yosry,

Thanks for taking a look at this series! I don't think we're able to
do this directly in lruvec_page_state()/lruvec_page_state_monotonic()
because I think there's still some places where the node stat and the
root memcg stat are not guaranteed to be equal.

The stat I was looking at last week was slab's NR_SLAB_RECLAIMABLE_B
and NR_SLAB_UNRECLAIMABLE_B where for those, the node counter value
can contain memory/stats that wasn't actually charged to any memcg,
which I think means for these cases, the node counter values can be
larger than what reading the root memcg rstat value would give. The
functions I was looking at were account_slab() and
memcg_slab_post_alloc_hook() where the logic adds every new slab page
to the node counter but the memcg stats only get updated if specific
criteria are met (eg the cache had SLAB_ACCOUNT set or the allocation
had the __GFP_ACCOUNT gfp flag set and the allocation was not from a
root memcg).

Thanks,
Joanne

reviews.author: Yosry Ahmed
reviews.summary: Reviewer suggested special casing slab stats to read from node counters by default, eliminating the need for a flush.
reviews.raw_body:
If it's only the slab stats, it probably makes sense to special case
those instead of the rest of the readers, right? It would be nice if
the default behavior is reading the node stats that doesn't require a
flush.

2026-11-02.patch_summary: This patch improves the accuracy of LRU (Least Recently Used) statistics in the Linux kernel's memory cgroup (memcg) subsystem by reading the root lruvec LRU stats from the node counters instead of relying on potentially stale rstat flushes. This change is particularly important for global reclaim and refault detection, where accurate statistics are crucial. The patch introduces two new functions, `lruvec_lru_page_state` and its monotonic variant, which read the node counters for the root memcg. This approach eliminates the latency introduced by rstat flushes, reducing the time taken to perform root reclaim from approximately 0.9ms to near-zero. The change also improves the accuracy of LRU statistics, ensuring that they reflect the current state of memory allocation and deallocation in the system.
